paper.title_en: Resolved $Q_1^q$-$Q_{7γ}$ interference in $\bar{B}\to X_sγ$ at NLO: Hard matching and radiative charm-loop jet function for $m_c \to 0$
paper.abstract_en: We study next-to-leading-order (NLO) QCD corrections to the subleading-power resolved-photon contribution to $\bar{B}\to X_sγ$ arising from the interference of the current-current operator $Q_1^q$ and the electromagnetic dipole operator $Q_{7γ}$. This contribution is among the main sources of theoretical uncertainty in Standard Model predictions for the decay rate. Using a factorisation theorem in soft-collinear effective theory for the kinematic endpoint region, $m_b-2E_γ=\mathcal{O}(Λ_{\rm QCD})$, we determine all previously unknown perturbative ingredients at NLO in the limit of a vanishing charm-quark mass, $m_c\to0$. Specifically, we compute the $m_c$-independent one-loop hard-matching coefficients, derive their renormalisation-group equations, and obtain accurate analytic approximations to their solutions by retaining the first two terms in a $1/N_c$ expansion. Our second main result is the two-loop correction to the radiative charm-loop jet function, including its full dependence on the collinear momentum fraction. Combining these results with the known $\mathcal{O}(α_s)$ correction to the quark jet function and the one-loop renormalisation of the subleading shape function $g_{17}$, previously computed by some of us, we provide the first complete NLO description of this resolved contribution in the massless-charm limit. This leaves the $m_c$ dependence of the radiative charm-loop jet function as the remaining ingredient for a phenomenological analysis within renormalisation-group-improved perturbation theory.
